subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 34-year-old woman with a 2-year history of episodic headache, palpitations, and diaphoresis is found to have paroxysmal hypertension to 210/120 mm Hg during an episode. A 24-hour urine collection shows increased fractionated metanephrines, and imaging shows a 3-cm left adrenal mass. She is scheduled for resection of a pheochromocytoma.
question: Which of the following enzymes catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the synthesis of the catecholamines stored in this tumor?
explanation_correct: Catecholamine synthesis begins with conversion of tyrosine to DOPA by tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting and regulated step, which requires tetrahydrobiopterin and iron. DOPA is then decarboxylated by a pyridoxal phosphate-dependent enzyme to dopamine, dopamine is hydroxylated by dopamine beta-hydroxylase (vitamin C) to norepinephrine, and norepinephrine is methylated by phenylethanolamine-N-methyltransferase (SAM) to epinephrine. The elevated metanephrines in this patient reflect catabolism of these amines.

explanation_incorrect.A: Phenylalanine hydroxylase converts phenylalanine to tyrosine and is deficient in phenylketonuria; it does not catalyze the rate-limiting step of catecholamine synthesis.
explanation_incorrect.C: DOPA decarboxylase carries out the second step and requires pyridoxal phosphate, but it is not the rate-limiting enzyme.
explanation_incorrect.D: Dopamine beta-hydroxylase converts dopamine to norepinephrine and requires vitamin C; it is not rate-limiting.
explanation_incorrect.E: Phenylethanolamine-N-methyltransferase performs the final methylation of norepinephrine to epinephrine and uses SAM, but it is not rate-limiting.

educationalObjective: Tyrosine hydroxylase catalyzes the rate-limiting, tetrahydrobiopterin-dependent step of catecholamine synthesis.
